segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices so that they could go and anoint him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And very early on the first day of the week they came to the tomb, when the sun had risen.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were saying to one another,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Who will roll the stone away from the entrance of the tomb for us?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And looking up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away, for it was extremely large.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Entering the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, dressed in a white robe, and they were alarmed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he said to them,

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: “Do not be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified. He has been raised; he is not here. Look, here is the place where they laid him.

segments.speaker: angel
segments.text: But go, tell his disciples and Peter, ‘He is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see him, just as he told you.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they went out and fled from the tomb, for trembling and astonishment had seized them; and they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid. ⟦And they briefly reported all that they had been commanded to Peter and those with him. And after this Jesus himself also sent out through them, from east to west, the sacred and imperishable proclamation of eternal salvation. Amen.⟧

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: ⟦Now after he rose early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had driven out seven demons.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: She went and reported it to those who had been with him, as they were mourning and weeping.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And when they heard that he was alive and had been seen by her, they did not believe it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After this he showed himself in a different form to two of them as they were walking, on their way into the country.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they went back and reported it to the rest; but they did not believe them either.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Later he showed himself to the eleven themselves as they were reclining at table, and he reproached them for their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they had not believed those who had seen him after he had been raised.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And these signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will drive out demons; they will speak in new languages;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: they will pick up snakes, and if they drink anything deadly it will not harm them at all; they will lay hands on the sick, and they will get well.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So then the Lord Jesus, after speaking to them, was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they went out and proclaimed everywhere, while the Lord worked with them and confirmed the word through the signs that followed.⟧

notes.phrase: the first day of the week
notes.traditional: the first day of the week
notes.note: Literally ‘on day one of the sabbaths.’ In Jewish Greek the plural ‘sabbaths’ could mean the week, and days were counted from the Sabbath, so this is the day after it, our Sunday. The Sabbath had ended at sunset the evening before, when the spices could be bought; the women come at first light.

Mark calls the figure simply a young man, and the translation keeps that. White clothing was the conventional dress of heavenly messengers in Jewish writing, and Matthew's parallel account calls him an angel outright. Nearly all interpreters take Mark to mean an angel, so his words are labelled as an angel's speech.

notes.traditional: He is risen / He has risen
notes.note: The Greek verb is passive in form. It can be read as a true passive, ‘he has been raised’ (that is, by God), or as an intransitive, ‘he has risen’; translations divide. The passive is chosen here because early Christian proclamation regularly says that God raised Jesus, but the other reading remains grammatically possible.

notes.phrase: And they briefly reported all that they had been commanded to Peter and those with him
notes.note: The double brackets mark text that the editors of the Greek edition judge not to be original to Mark. The two earliest Greek manuscripts of Mark, both from the fourth century, end at ‘for they were afraid.’ The bracketed sentences here, known as the shorter ending, appear in a small number of manuscripts, usually followed by verses 9–20, and their vocabulary is unlike Mark's. Whether Mark meant to end at ‘for they were afraid’ or an original ending was lost is disputed.
The adverb can mean ‘concisely’ (of speech) or ‘promptly’ (of time). English translations divide between the two, and either fits the sentence.

Literally ‘those around Peter.’ In Greek of this period the idiom commonly includes the named person together with his circle, and it is rendered that way here. Some translations keep the literal wording, which could be heard as leaving Peter out.

notes.phrase: Now after he rose early on the first day of the week
notes.note: The double brackets around verses 9–20, the longer ending, mark them as a later addition in the editors' judgment. They are found in the great majority of manuscripts and were known by the late second century, but they are absent from the two earliest Greek manuscripts, and Eusebius and Jerome report that they were missing from most copies known to them. The style differs from the rest of Mark, and Mary Magdalene is introduced as if for the first time. Most scholars regard the passage as an early summary of resurrection appearances attached to the Gospel.

‘Gospel’ is now a religious term or the name of a book. The Greek was an ordinary word for a public announcement of good news, also used of imperial proclamations. Many modern translations already alternate between ‘good news’ and ‘gospel.’

The Greek word means the tongue as an organ and, by extension, a language; ‘tongues’ in the traditional rendering is simply older English for ‘languages.’ ‘Languages’ is used here because ‘tongues’ has become a technical religious term. What kind of speech is meant, whether foreign languages as in Acts 2 or the ecstatic speech discussed in 1 Corinthians, is left open by the Greek.

notes.phrase: sat down at the right hand of God
notes.note: The seat at a king's right hand was the place of highest honour and shared authority. The wording echoes Psalm 110:1 (‘Sit at my right hand’), the Scripture text most often applied to Jesus by the first Christians, and ‘taken up into heaven’ recalls the language used of Elijah.
